title: Work IQ: agents select the most relevant skills for each request
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents an API for changing package user availability, which the briefing reports as undocumented. The briefing also unnecessarily treats Work IQ's platform-wide user-permission boundary as unconfirmed for this Work IQ feature.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: User availability for a selected plugin or standalone skill package can be all users, no users, or specific users and groups.
claims.quote: Manage user availability | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. | Make the package available to all users, no users, or specific users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: API operations and user availability
claims.claim: No API is documented for setting skill-package user availability.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated. allowedUsersAndGroups: Users/groups for whom the package is available. availableTo: Enum value specifying which users or groups within the tenant can access this package.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind graph, call 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} with JSON body {"availableTo":"allowedForNone"}', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackagedetail-update; mirror it in the rendered table. Add to the row note 'Example makes the package unavailable to all users; beta API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.' Replace the sentence claiming no user-availability operation with 'The beta Update package operation updates user availability through availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups.' The resource reference documents allowedForAll, allowedForSome and allowedForNone; availableTo is required when updating allowedUsersAndGroups.
